news.Title: Amazon's Report Passed Both Tests I Set for It. I'd Buy More of the Stock Now.
news.Content:
Shares of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) trade around $250 as I write, more than 10% under their Aug. 3 closing high of $284.02. And they dipped after the company's third-quarter report on Oct. 29, even though Amazon had the highest operating margin in its history.

Before that report, I said I'd buy half a position ahead of it and the other half after. I also listed what would make me skip the second half: growth at Amazon Web Services (AWS) dropping back toward 20%, or operating income landing below management's guided range of $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Neither happened. AWS grew 39%, and operating income was $28.1 billion. But the report also showed how fast the cost of that growth is climbing.

Image source: Getty Images.

AWS: six straight quarters of faster growth

AWS, Amazon's cloud computing unit, is the company's profit engine. AWS revenue climbed 39% year over year to $46.0 billion for the third quarter. Growth has now picked up for six straight quarters, from 17% for the first quarter of 2025 to 18%, 20%, 24%, 28%, 37%, and now 39%. For a business with an annualized revenue run rate of $184 billion, I think this pace is remarkable.

AWS operating income climbed 55% to $17.8 billion, and the segment's operating margin widened to 38.7% from 34.6% for the third quarter of 2025. Sure, this margin did dip a little from the second quarter's 39.4%.

But the forward-looking number points the other way. AWS's backlog (customer commitments it hasn't yet booked as revenue) hit $578 billion, more than doubling year over year. And management said it thinks AWS can grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

Profits grew, just not 61%

Amazon's third-quarter operating income of $28.1 billion was up 61% from $17.4 billion a year ago, and it landed above even the top of the range management had guided to. Its operating margin of 13.9% compares to 9.7% for the year-ago quarter.

But the 61% number flatters the trend. Amazon's year-ago results included two special charges -- $2.5 billion for a legal settlement with the Federal Trade Commission and $1.8 billion in estimated severance costs. Without them, third-quarter 2025 operating income would have been $21.7 billion. By that measure, operating income grew around 29%.

Story Continues

It's still an impressive rate for a business with almost $800 billion in sales over the last 12 months. And the retail side pulled its weight. North America segment operating income climbed to $8.7 billion from $7.3 billion a year earlier excluding the settlement charge, or around 20% growth on sales that climbed 6%.

The AI bill keeps rising

Amazon's cash capital expenditures (spending on data centers, servers, chips, and warehouses) hit $75.9 billion in the third quarter alone, over twice the year-ago number. Management still expects around $220 billion for 2026, up from about $128 billion in 2025.

"[E]xpect to spend meaningfully more in 2027 with a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns," CEO Andy Jassy said on the third-quarter earnings call.

This spending has turned Amazon's free cash flow into a big outflow. For the past 12 months, free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion, compared to negative $7.6 billion through the second quarter and positive $14.8 billion a year before. Operating cash flow, meanwhile, grew 29% to $168.3 billion over the past 12 months.

In other words, the company is taking in more cash than ever. Amazon is just spending more than all of it, mainly because of the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. True, a $578 billion backlog arguably makes that spending look less like a gamble. But free cash flow could stay negative for a while if spending grows again in 2027, and I see that as the main risk with the stock.

I'd buy the second half now

The report didn't change my plan. Both things I said would decide the second half came through.

At around $250, Amazon's price-to-earnings ratio on analysts' 2027 estimates is about 23, down from about 24 when I spelled out the plan in late October. For a business whose underlying operating income rose about 29%, that valuation looks fair, even if the price still assumes the AI spending eventually turns into cash.

I'd go ahead and buy the second half of the position here. I'd just expect the free cash flow numbers to look rough for a while.

news.Title: 日本東京、中部電力現貨價創4年新高，日股週二因文化日休市
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】燃料成本上升推高日本電力批發價格，東京及中部地區日前成交的次日交割電力現貨價，分別達每度36.11日圓及36.29日圓，創2022年9月以來新高。兩地價格較一週前分別上漲1.1%及7.2%，反映能源成本壓力持續傳導至電力市場。上述價格為11月1日交易、11月2日交割的電力，並非家庭用戶直接支付的每度電價。日本發電結構對進口燃料依賴度高。根據日本資源能源廳資料，液化天然氣(LNG)燃氣發電約占全國發電量三成，使電力成本容易受到國際天然氣價格及供應變化影響。中東局勢推升燃料成本之際，東京與中部電力現貨價同步走高，增加電力採購端的成本壓力。

不過，電力現貨市場價格波動與家庭電費調整，屬於不同層次的價格變化，不能將每度36日圓以上的批發報價直接視為居民電價。市場追蹤資料顯示，11月3日交割的東京地區電力現貨日均價已回落至每度31.11日圓，反映短期報價仍會波動，單日高點也不代表後續價格必然持續攀升。

交易安排方面，日本股票市場週二(3日)適逢文化日休市一天，週三恢復交易。

news.Title: Why RH Stock Jumped 20% in October
news.Content: Shares of RH (NYSE:RH), the high-end home-furnishing company formerly known as Restoration Hardware, were moving higher last month on a broad upswing in housing stocks. Interest rates started to edge lower. The Federal Reserve declined to raise the benchmark Federal funds rate, and investors rotated out of AI stocks , landing on housing stocks as one of several potential opportunities. RH also seemed to benefit from a short squeeze , as the stock had become heavily shorted after several quarters of sluggish growth. As of Oct. 15, 58% of the float was sold short. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » There was little company-specific news out on RH last month, but the rally in the housing sector was clear, and it was enough to lift the stock 20%, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence . As you can see from the chart below, RH stock started moving late in the month as interest rates fell. Notably, the stock also moved up as the S&P 500 went down, showing what appeared to be a rotation out of AI stocks and into the housing sector. RH data by YCharts Why RH suddenly popped Starting on Oct. 20, a combination of a short squeeze and a broader rotation into housing stocks seemed to lift RH shares. The stock jumped 5% on Oct. 20, another 7% on Oct. 21 on high volume, and then popped 9.4% on its highest daily volume since its earnings report on Oct. 22, indicating a possible short squeeze. After a brief pullback, the stock rallied again into the end of the month. On Oct. 22, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note also fell sharply, closing at 4.95%, down 3.8% and its first close below 5% in a month. That move was a response to fears about AI spending, seen in Meta's first quarter of negative free cash flow in its earnings report the night before. It also signaled a rotation out of AI stocks and into bonds. That pattern continued through the end of the month as tech stocks and Treasury yields fell and RH stock moved higher. Image source: Getty Images. What's next for RH RH delivered better-than-expected results in its most recent earnings report as the company now sees full-year revenue growth of 5.5%-7%, even as it continues to open new galleries and pushes forward in Europe. It will take a significant recovery in the housing market to accelerate the company's growth and boost its margins, but that will come at some point. While the Fed is not expected to lower rates, market dynamics change quickly, and investors seem to think the housing sector has rebound potential. Story Continues Investors will have to be patient with RH stock, but if momentum returns to the business, it has a lot of upside potential. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook. Continue » Jeremy Bowman has positions in RH. The Motley Fool recommends RH. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy . Why RH Stock Jumped 20% in October was originally published by The Motley Fool

news.Title: 統一證券：台股靜待籌碼沉澱後，醞釀築底反彈
news.Content:
【昨日盤勢】：

Intel受記憶體缺貨影響PC終端售價，導致買氣極凍影響，財測疲弱而暴跌28%；同時AI資本支出不斷攀升，自由現金流量轉負，引發資本市場質疑AI供應鏈變現能力與投資報酬率，影響全球科技股持續承壓。台股週一維持弱勢震盪，隨聯發科及鴻海由黑翻紅，加權指數跌幅收斂。電子族群以面板、玻纖布及資訊服務表現較為強勢；傳產則為電線電纜及造紙股避險買盤增溫。權值股方面，台積電下跌1.69%、鴻海上漲2.24%、聯發科上漲1.40%、廣達收平盤，台達電上漲1.50%。盤面強勢股，富喬、建榮、大世科、華經、威鋒電子、同欣電等共41檔漲停；豐達科、中釉、大同、驊宏資、超豐、眾達-KY等漲幅5%以上。盤面弱勢股，博磊、新代、意藍、禾伸堂、泓德能源等9檔個股跌停；嘉基、律勝、大甲、華新科、晶豪科、佳世達等跌幅5%以上。終場台灣加權指數下跌291.69點，以44920.14點作收，成交量7588.75億元。觀察盤面變化，三大類股漲跌互見，電子下跌0.81%、傳產上漲0.78%、金融下跌1.00%。在次族群部份，以油燃、電纜、造紙表現較佳，分別上漲4.26%、3.26%、2.22%。

【資金動向】：

三大法人合計賣超549.93億元。其中外資賣超735.21億元，投信買超338.16億元，自營商賣超152.88億元。外資買超前五大為群創、鴻海、華航、友達、中鋼；賣超前五大為力積電、台積電、台新新光金、富喬、永豐金。投信買超前五大為台新新光金、中信金、永豐金、日月光投控、玉山金；賣超前五大為聯電、新纖、華星光、友達、兆豐金。資券變化方面，融資減7.69億元，融資餘額為6226.99億元，融券減0.24萬張，融券餘額為19.49萬張。外資台指期部位，空單減少2862口，淨空單部位89379口，借券賣出金額335.64億元。類股成交比重：電子85.43%、傳產11.13%、金融3.43%。

【今日盤勢分析】：

美伊有望重啟和平談判，帶動油價大跌。Apple 第三季（即其會計年度第四季）營收為1,145億美元，優於華爾街預期，但在中國業績明顯不如預期，蘋果盤後股價跌逾2%。另外，記憶體大廠鎧俠獲利展望不如預期，加深市場對記憶體業獲利成長能否延續的疑慮。週一美股四大指數漲跌互見，台積電ADR下跌1.85%，台指期夜盤下跌2.03%。台股後市分析如下：

第一、邁威爾Marvell Technology宣布，將以全股票交易方式收購光通訊元件供應商Lumentum，交易企業價值達1,150億美元。此次收購Lumentum將使Marvell從AI晶片及網路技術進一步延伸至光學元件製造，但在交易規模大幅提高後，如何將光通訊需求成長轉化為足以支撐收購成本的獲利，將成為市場後續觀察重點。

第二、AI推動先進製程需求強勁，矽晶圓市況比預期強，現階段客戶拉貨力道優於預期，部分原本要在2027年初出貨的訂單也提早一季開始拉貨。矽晶圓市況復甦動能優於預期，環球晶、台勝科、合晶等台廠營運同步熱轉。

第三、技術面觀察，週一加權指數量縮仍失守半年線。技術指標，KD、RSI持續向下，MACD維持綠柱體，整體技術面弱勢整理，且進入超跌區。現階段靜待國際股市轉佳，後續觀察費半、那指、台積電走勢及外資期現貨態度，視為醞釀跌深反彈指標。OTC指數回測年線，非基本面支撐的中小型股須留意法人動態。

第四、盤面資金聚焦玻纖布、面板、資訊服務、電線電纜等族群，包括富喬、群創、華經、華新等表現強勢。

【投資策略】：

儘管國際油價回落，市場將焦點轉向本週科技財報及美國期中選舉。回歸台股，本周上市櫃公司陸續公布營收，AI供應鏈可望持續繳出佳績，惟目前融資減幅小於大盤回檔跌幅，靜待籌碼沉澱後，醞釀築底反彈。根據統計美期中選舉後，美股上漲機率高，操作建議保持資金彈性，避免過度槓桿，逢回布局，AI概念及業績題材股，搭配短期營收動能股，長線追蹤族群：台積電及先進封測、PCB供應鏈、光傳輸、散熱、貨櫃散裝、特用化學及金融股等。

資料來源- MoneyDJ理財網

news.Title: 5 Key Earnings Charts to Watch This Week
news.Content:
Third quarter earnings season is moving beyond the Magnificent 7 as only NVIDIA remains still to report earnings. This week there will be over 1,000 companies reporting earnings, including small and mid-cap companies that investors often overlook.

Technology will remain in focus but we're also going to hear from many consumer-focused companies including restaurants, travel, beauty, and apparel companies.

So far, earnings reports have been better-than-expected at many of the consumer-focused companies including the cruise lines and hotel chains.

Will that continue this week?

Having a Perfect Earnings Surprise Record Isn't Easy

Two of the key companies to watch this week have perfect 5-year earnings surprise streaks. That means it has met or beat on earnings every quarter since the end of 2021. That's impressive.

How does a company get such a record? It usually means management is good at communicating with the covering analysts each quarter about what is going on at the company.

It's not easy beating on earnings for years. But these companies are doing that.

Will we see another earnings beat this quarter?

5 Key Earnings Charts to Watch This Week

1. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. ( AMD )

Advanced Micro Devices is an earnings all-star. It hasn't missed on earnings in the last five years. That is perfection.

However, shares of Advanced Micro Devices are down 26% in the last month on the AI sell-off. Earnings are expected to rise 81% in Fiscal 2026 after jumping 26% in Fiscal 2025.

Is this a buying opportunity in Advanced Micro Devices?

2. McDonald's Corp. ( MCD )

McDonald's has beat on earnings three out of the last four quarters. It has a good long-term earnings track record. McDonald's has only missed four times in the last five years.

Shares of McDonald's have slid 13% year-to-date on worries over consumer spending. It's not that cheap, however. McDonald's still trades with a forward P/E of 20.

Will this be the quarter that McDonald's turns it around?

3. Expedia Group, Inc. ( EXPE )

Expedia has beat on earnings five quarters in a row. It also has an excellent longer track record with just three misses over the last five years.

Shares of Expedia are up in the last month, gaining 12.8%, on signs that the consumer is still traveling. Expedia is cheap, with a forward P/E of just 14. A P/E under 15 usually signals the company has value.

Will Expedia beat on earnings again this week?

4. e.l.f. Beauty, Inc. ( ELF )

e.l.f. Beauty has only missed on earnings one time in the last 5 years and it was in 2025. It has put together a streak of 6 earnings beats in a row.

Story Continues

Beauty seems to be gaining momentum. Shares of e.l.f. Beauty are up 45% year-to-date. However, e.l.f. Beauty isn't cheap, with a forward P/E of 30. A P/E above 25 is usually considered to be an expensive stock.

Is beauty and e.l.f. Beauty back on track to end 2026?

5. Ralph Lauren Corp. ( RL )

news.Title: Nvidia Reports Nov. 17. History Says What Its Stock Usually Does Next.
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) will report results for the three months ended Oct. 25 (its fiscal third quarter of 2027) after the close on Tuesday, Nov. 17. As of this writing, shares sit near $205, putting the stock about 14% under its Oct. 6 closing high of $239.24.

Investors hoping a strong report can push the stock back toward its record might want to see how the artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant's shares have reacted lately. In all of Nvidia's past 10 reports, going back to May 2024, revenue beat the top of the range management had forecast. But the stock fell the next trading day after six of those.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Still, I don't think this record is much of a reason to avoid the stock before the report.

Image source: Nvidia.

Six drops in 10 reports

Because Nvidia 's reports come out after trading ends for the day, the easiest way to gauge the move is from the report-day close to the next day's close. On that basis, the worst day of the stretch was in February 2025.

The stock dropped around 8.5% after a fiscal fourth-quarter report with revenue up 78% year over year to $39.3 billion. That was almost $2 billion more than the $37.5 billion management had guided for.

The pattern carried into 2026. Nvidia's revenue for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter was $68.1 billion in February, over the company's $65.0 billion forecast, and shares dropped around 5% the next day. In May, fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $81.6 billion beat a $78.0 billion forecast, and the stock dipped around 2%. With the drops after the August and November 2025 reports, that was four straight.

Yet August's report snapped the streak. Revenue for the fiscal second quarter more than doubled, up 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, well above the $91.0 billion outlook. And the stock climbed around 9% the next day.

Over all 10 reports, shares moved about 5% up or down on average.

There's no simple pattern in which way they went, either. The February 2025 drop came with a forecast for Nvidia's gross margin to dip to 70.6% from 73%. But August's report also called for a lower gross margin (74%, down from 75%), and the stock climbed.

Of course, the stock's other big gain in the stretch, around 9% in May 2024, followed the same report in which Nvidia announced a 10-for-1 stock split.

Story Continues

Most drops didn't last

For a long-term shareholder, what came after the first day counts more. Here, Nvidia's record looks far better.

After five of the six drops, shares were back above their report-day close by the time Nvidia next reported, around three months later. After the February 2026 fall, for example, the stock rose about 21% from its post-report close by the May 20 report.

The only exception was May 2026. Shares dipped around 2% the day after the report and were about 6% under their report-day close by the time the August report arrived.

The record can go the other way, too. All of the 9% rise after August's report has since faded. As of this writing, shares are around 10% below where they closed the day after that report.

Time to buy before Nov. 17?

Nvidia is guiding for fiscal third-quarter revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. If it hits the midpoint, revenue would climb around 89% from the $57.0 billion Nvidia pulled in for the same quarter last year.

True, growth at that rate would be a slowdown from the 106% Nvidia posted in its fiscal second quarter. And shares could easily fall again on Nov. 18, the first trading day after the report. Going by the latest 10 reports, a drop is arguably a bit more likely than a rise.

But the stock's valuation already looks reasonable.

Analysts' consensus is for around $15.80 in earnings per share for fiscal 2028, which ends in January 2028. Using that figure, the stock trades at around 14 times earnings. That's a modest price for a company whose revenue more than doubled year over year in its latest quarter.

So, does history say to wait for the report before buying? I don't think so. The day after has tilted negative. But most of those drops didn't last, and Nvidia has kept topping its own revenue forecasts. I'd consider buying shares before Nov. 17 rather than guessing the next day's move.

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be SpaceX’s Stock Price by the End of 2027
news.Content:
Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) has had an eventful first four months on the stock market. But the company hasn't made much money for investors who have held on since its debut. As of writing, SpaceX's shares are trading at $134 each, below the company's IPO price of $135. Still, SpaceX boasts attractive opportunities. How will the company perform over the next year? Let's try to determine what its share price might be by the end of 2027.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Revenue and profit drivers

SpaceX's financial results have been strong this year. In the third quarter, the company's revenue grew by 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. It also posted a net income of $4.4 billion -- or $0.35 per diluted share -- substantially better than the prior-year quarter's net loss of $1.1 billion (or $0.36 per share).

SpaceX's annual revenue run rate is now at $58.4 billion. Analysts expect the company's total revenue for the current fiscal year to be $48.93 billion (according to Yahoo! Finance), and its earnings per share (EPS) to be $0.22, as of this writing. What about next year? Analysts are projecting $180.37 billion in revenue and $4.03 in EPS, on average.

Note that at current levels, SpaceX is trading at about 33.3x projected 2027 earnings, which seems reasonable for a company growing as fast as it is. But there is a complication. These projections may already be baked into the share price. After all, despite excellent financial results for as long as it has been public, SpaceX stock has gone nowhere.

The question, then, is whether SpaceX will perform roughly in line with, above, or below expectations over the next 12 months. Let's consider the bullish case first. SpaceX's artificial intelligence segment, dubbed Super Intelligence (SI), is booming. The company has more demand for AI compute capacity than it is willing to rent out. Third-quarter SI revenue soared 830% year over year to $7.6 billion. Perhaps the market is underestimating the company's potential in this industry.

The SI segment could maintain outstanding growth provided SpaceX adds more compute deals to its portfolio. Connectivity is also performing. SpaceX's push into additional regions within this market could deliver significant subscription growth. Then there is SpaceX's space segment.

Story Continues

This unit isn't profitable, but progress on the company's Starship rocket could be key over the next year. If Starship launch cadence improves meaningfully within the next year, and there are no significant issues with the rocket -- regulatory or otherwise -- that could be a massive catalyst for the stock.

There are plenty of possible outcomes

The bull scenario might convince the market that SpaceX's prospects beyond 2027 are very attractive, allowing the company to continue to command high earnings multiples. Assuming the fiscal year 2026 and 2027 predictions are correct, along with a constant forward P/E (based on the following year's earnings) and projected 2028 EPS of $7.01, the stock could soar by about 74% to $233 by the end of 2027.

In my view, that's too optimistic. Several factors might hinder SpaceX's prospects. Revenue and earnings growth could normalize after their blistering recent pace. Launch cadence for SpaceX's Starship might not reach the levels the market expects, and competition across the company's business will intensify. That last point is important.

Nobody should expect one of SpaceX's competitors to catch up to the company in the space launch or connectivity markets within the next year. Still, if they make significant progress, the rocket company might no longer command the same kind of valuation premium. If we make just one change to our model and assume, instead, that the company's forward P/E drops to 25, SpaceX could gain 31% by the end of 2027. Under this scenario, the company's share price will be $175.25.

That's much closer to what may happen, in my view, but here's the problem: SpaceX's prospects look attractive, but they are also incredibly uncertain. Beyond the variables already discussed, there is the very real possibility that SpaceX will seek to acquire Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) within the next year. We can't be sure, and there is no official announcement yet.

But CEO Elon Musk himself has said it would be a good idea and has indicated the formation of independent special committees to weigh the pros and cons of a potential merger between the two companies.

Will a merger be announced? If it is, how much regulatory scrutiny and public backlash will it attract? Nobody knows the answer to these questions yet. With all this uncertainty, SpaceX may well deliver outstanding returns through the end of 2027 or beyond, but it might also be a wealth destroyer. I'd like a much bigger margin of error before buying the stock.

news.Title: AMD Reports Tuesday. Here's the Number That Will Show Whether It's Gaining on Nvidia
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, and the stock is heading in on a shaky note. Shares fell nearly 11% on Friday and sold off further on Monday amid broader chip stock weakness, with no AMD-specific news. In all, AMD is down nearly 30% from its all-time high, reached less than a month ago.

Of course, we have no idea what AMD will report, but the headline results probably won't be the surprise. AMD guided for revenue of about $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, and analysts expect $13.09 billion, which would be 41.5% higher than a year ago.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The guidance is the real story

The more important figure is likely to be AMD's fourth-quarter guidance, and specifically how much of it comes from data center GPUs. AMD began shipping its Helios rack-scale systems, built on its MI450 chips, in September, so the third quarter won't include a full period of its volume. However, management said on its last call that it expects the ramp to accelerate meaningfully in the fourth quarter.

The average estimate among Wall Street analysts is about $16.3 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, and Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis expects closer to $17 billion. A forecast at or above that higher level would suggest Helios demand is turning into revenue at an impressive pace. AMD has plenty of big customers lined up, including OpenAI, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Anthropic, so expectations are high.

AMD doesn't need to catch Nvidia

To put AMD's AI business in perspective, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) generated $89 billion of data center revenue in its most recent quarter. AMD's entire data center segment, which includes its EPYC server processors, generated $6.7 billion in revenue. AMD isn't going to close that gap anytime soon.

However, it doesn't need to. AI companies want a second source of computing power so they aren't completely dependent on one supplier, and AMD has emerged as the most credible alternative. CEO Lisa Su has said each gigawatt of AI capacity represents double-digit billions in revenue, so even a modest share of the market would be an enormous win.

Of course, there are risks to watch. For example, AI chips carry slightly lower margins than server processors, so a fast GPU ramp could weigh on gross margin. It's also worth noting that Intel 's (NASDAQ:INTC) warning about a shrinking PC market could also be a headwind for AMD's client business, which grew 23% last quarter.

Story Continues

In short, I'm watching the guidance more than the results. If the fourth-quarter outlook shows Helios ramping up on schedule, the recent pullback could be a buying opportunity for long-term investors in an excellent AI stock.

news.Title: AI Earnings: 3 Reports to Watch This Week

Concerns surrounding stretched valuations and the overall return on AI investments have been major contributors to the weakness, with investors seemingly becoming more selective despite the continued growth story.

Given the recent volatility, this week's earnings releases from Super Micro Computer SMCI, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, and Arm Holdings ARM will undoubtedly be closely watched, particularly concerning the overall AI demand picture.

Let's take a closer look at a few key metrics to watch in each release.

Growth expectations remain sizable, with the Zacks Consensus Estimate calling for $15.7 billion in sales and earnings of $1.24 per share, reflecting 214% and 254% YoY growth, respectively.

Our latest Zacks Consensus estimates call for $13.1 billion in sales and earnings of $1.94 per share, reflecting 42% revenue growth on 62% higher earnings. Beyond Data Center sales, investors should watch commentary on its next-generation AI accelerators, customer adoption, and the overall GPU demand pipeline.

Arm Holdings

Current analyst consensus estimates call for roughly $1.4 billion in sales and earnings of $0.48 per share, suggesting 21% revenue growth on 23% higher earnings. Royalty revenue will be a major focus, particularly concerning the growing adoption of Arm-based processors in cloud infrastructure. AI-related earnings remain a major theme throughout the current reporting cycle, with Super Micro Computer SMCI, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, and Arm Holdings ARM all gearing up for releases this week.

Beyond the headline results, commentary surrounding AI demand, customer adoption, and forward guidance will be critical in determining whether their impressive growth trajectories can continue.

news.Title: Micron Technology: Is This a Sign That Its Stock Has Already Peaked?
news.Content:
Earlier in the year, it looked as though Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) stock was unstoppable. It was soaring as demand for memory was through the roof, and the company was able to hike prices, benefiting from stronger margins and sky-high demand. Its numbers have been unreal, making it a must-buy for many growth investors.

But in recent months, that hasn't been the case. Even though the tech stock is trading at a low earnings multiple, investors haven't been taking the bait. And there could be another indication that the tech stock may have peaked: trading volumes are down significantly.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Micron.

Has the interest in Micron faded?

When a stock is a hot buy with retail investors, trading volumes are through the roof, and that can send it to astronomical heights. Micron hit a milestone earlier this year, crossing $1 trillion in market cap. But it's now below that threshold, trading closer to a market cap of about $940 billion. It's still massive, but it's down significantly from the highs it reached during the summer.

A big telltale sign that the stock may have already peaked is its 30-day average trading volume. It's down significantly. The chart below shows that as it hit its high around late June, volumes were also up considerably.

MU 30-Day Average Daily Volume data by YCharts

Theoretically, news that the memory shortage will last longer than expected could draw interest, potentially give the stock a bigger boost, and attract more investors. However, there have been multiple reports of the shortage lasting for years, and many investors aren't willing to shake concerns that more supply could come online in the near future, earlier than expected. Or perhaps they simply want to cash out before it's too late, especially with the stock sitting on massive gains -- more than 1,000% in five years.

I wouldn't buy Micron's stock, even while it's trading lower

The risk with volatile and historically cyclical stocks like Micron is that, while they can be hot buys when things are going well and there are shortages, they can quickly become the stocks no one wants to own when the bubble has burst and more supply comes online.

While Micron's earnings multiple of 11 may look enticingly low, it's skewed based on recent results which have been incredibly strong. Odds are, those numbers won't be sustainable over the longer term, and when prices inevitably come down, the stock price could crash even quicker.

Story Continues

With so many growth stocks trading lower these days, there are plenty of good options to pursue that don't come with nearly as much uncertainty and risk as Micron, which is why I wouldn't bother with it.

news.Title: Marvell Technology Is Acquiring Lumentum. Why Does the Market Hate the Move?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) just announced a huge move. It's acquiring Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in a deal that values the tech company at a whopping $115 billion, based on implied enterprise value. It's a move that will expand the company's growth opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI) and bolster its total addressable market to $550 billion.

But the tech stock is down sharply on the news, hitting levels it hasn't seen in several months. Why does the market not appear to like this move, and could buying Marvell's stock on the dip be a good idea right now?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

The deal is a big bet on AI

Marvell announced on Monday that it would acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction valued at $115 billion. Management sees this as a way to create a "category leader in AI connectivity," with Lumentum making optical products essential to the AI infrastructure build-out. By combining chips with optical connections, Marvell CEO Matt Murphy plans to build solutions "that are highly sticky."

The market, however, may not be thrilled with the massive price tag for Lumentum, nor with the all-stock offering, which will be dilutive to existing shareholders. It comes down to whether the net effect will prove to be a positive one for Marvell and lead to more earnings growth as a result of this combination, but based on the stock's performance, the market doesn't appear convinced of the payoff.

It also comes at a time when tech stocks have come under pressure of late. Marvell's pursuit of a significant purchase such as this may simply have come at a bad time. However, it's not unusual for shares of an acquiring company to fall in value when news of an acquisition comes out, as investors often question the value they are getting back in the deal, and whether it will pay off in the end.

Why Marvell's stock could still go lower

Marvell is making a big bet on the future demand for AI infrastructure, and the market may be unsure about that right now. With interest rates on the rise again, tech spending may slow in the near future.

Meanwhile, with Marvell's stock trading at around 60 times its trailing earnings, it was already a high-priced investment before this latest announcement. For investors who may have been thinking twice about the AI stock , Marvell may have given those on the fence a stronger reason to sell rather than buy, and this may just be the beginning of a bigger decline to come.

Story Continues

news.Title: Tesla Has a Flying Car. What Does This Mean for Archer's Flying "Taxi" Business?
news.Content:
A few weeks ago, a Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) Roadster drove up a nearly vertical ramp, turned upside down, then fell -- I mean, launched itself -- into the air before its side thrusters kicked in, flipping the car upright and landing it on the road below. It was by far the most incredible maneuver I've ever seen a car pull off. The Tesla then drove out of a cloud of vapor as if nothing had happened.

If you haven't seen Tesla's new flying car, it's worth watching the video (in another stunt, the car launches itself upside down and literally barrel-rolls over five vehicles before landing upright). It's an extraordinary demonstration of engineering, and one of those rare glimpses of a future that, until recently, seemed firmly in the realm of science fiction.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But now, what does this mean for Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR)? After all, Archer has also spent years developing its own flying vehicle -- an electric air taxi. If Tesla can make a flying car, will there still be a market for Archer's flying taxi, assuming it can get it certified? Let's take a look.

Tesla's flying car is stunning, but it's not a threat to Archer

I'll just come out and say it: I don't think Tesla's flying Roadster will have an impact on Archer .

For starters, Tesla isn't really competing with Archer. Look at what Tesla is making: A sports car -- a really sleek and aesthetically striking sports car -- that can burst briefly into flight. In contrast, Archer is building an eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) vehicle that can take off and land vertically like a helicopter and transition into forward flight like a traditional airplane. It's also an engineering feat, and unlike Tesla's Roadster, it doesn't need thrusters to launch into the air.

These are obviously different vehicles, built for different purposes. And between the two, Archer's is more practical. It's designed to carry four passengers and a pilot. The Roadster, on the other hand, can only carry one person.

Archer's aircraft is also likely closer to real-world use than Tesla's. The flying Roadster might be functional, but it's not approved for road use. There's some question as to whether Tesla could ever get regulatory approval to mass-produce a flying Roadster, but even if it did, it would likely not beat Archer to the punch. Archer has already completed three of the FAA's four type-certification phases and is now working through the final one.

Story Continues

Don't get me wrong, though: Tesla's recent demonstration was very impressive. But it was only impressive as a spectacle, not something that could solve transportation problems, like congested metropolitan roads. Archer's eVTOL, on the other hand, could alleviate traffic in some areas.

In sum, I don't believe Tesla's flying car changes much for Archer Aviation's future. If anything, it could even increase publicity around flying cars, helping Archer's air taxi services when it does get its eVTOL certified.

news.Title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 2: Marvell Announces $115 Billion All-Stock Acquisition of Lumentum
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a data infrastructure chipmaker for AI data centers, closed at $170.80, down 13%. The blockbuster announcement that the company was acquiring Lumentum sent shares lower, and investors are watching financing and integration risks next.

Trading volume reached 60.5 million shares, coming in about 171% above its three-month average of 22.3 million shares. Marvell Technology IPO'd in 2000 and has grown 1,111% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,542, down 0.50%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) finished at 25,164, down 1.07%. In the semiconductors for data infrastructure sector, Broadcom closed at $322.23, down 1.18%, while Lumentum finished at $684.40, down 18.59% after the deal headlines.

What this means for investors

On Monday, Marvell Technology announced a $115 billion all-stock agreement to buy Lumentum, a manufacturer of critical optical communications components, network modules, and commercial lasers for efficient data transmission. The acquisition is intended to boost Marvell's data center offerings to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom.

Last week, reports that Marvell was in advanced talks to buy Lumentum caused shares to slide as investors evaluated execution risk and capital allocation. Now that the deal has been announced, the market is weighing dilution, valuation, and financing risk.

Marvell CEO Matt Murphy explained the rationale for the acquisition, stating, "AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation."

Marvell was already on a path toward massive growth. During its Investor Day on Oct. 6, the company raised its revenue outlook for its 2028 fiscal year (FY), ended Jan. 31, 2028, to $20 billion, and set a FY2031 target of $70 billion to $90 billion in sales. Adding Lumentum could be a game changer, as tech giants spend billions of dollars to build data centers capable of rapid computational processing in support of increasingly complex AI systems.
