news.Title: Can Advanced Packaging Demand Drive KLAC's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
KLA Corporation KLAC is seeing strong demand for its process control products as AI infrastructure investment increases the need for advanced semiconductors. As chips become more complex, manufacturers need better inspection and measurement tools to identify defects and improve production yields. Advanced packaging is becoming an important growth driver for KLAC, as new chip designs require more sophisticated manufacturing processes.

KLAC expects revenues from its advanced packaging process control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion or more in 2026, suggesting growth of more than 70% year over year. This is nearly twice the expected growth rate of the advanced packaging market. The company is benefiting from the growing use of advanced packaging in AI infrastructure. Packaging technologies are also adopting more complex wafer manufacturing processes, which increase the need for KLAC's inspection and measurement solutions.

Demand for more advanced inspection tools is also increasing. Hybrid bonding and complex logic devices require higher inspection sensitivity to identify smaller defects. KLAC is seeing demand shift toward more advanced systems, including laser scanning and Gen 4 tools, while its macro inspection products continue to serve as key solutions. The company believes its existing technology portfolio and research and development investments position it well to meet these changing customer needs.

Looking ahead, KLAC expects its advanced packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027. Strong AI infrastructure investment and rising chip complexity should support demand for its process control solutions. As of now, the company will need to manage supply constraints and increase production capacity to meet customer requirements. Overall, advanced packaging is emerging as an important growth driver for KLAC and could support its broader growth outlook over the next few years.

KLAC Faces Tough Competition

Onto Innovation ONTO is seeing strong demand for its advanced packaging inspection and metrology solutions as AI chip designs become more complex. In the second quarter of 2026, Onto Innovation's revenues increased 35% year over year to $343 million, while its inspection business grew 30% sequentially, driven by 2.5D logic and high-bandwidth memory applications. The company raised its 2026 advanced packaging growth outlook to approximately 80%, up from its previous expectation of 50%.

Applied Materials AMAT is also benefiting from increased investment in advanced packaging. news.Title: Applied Materials, Inc. (AMAT) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
news.Content:
Applied Materials (AMAT) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Over the past month, shares of this maker of chipmaking equipment have returned -20.3%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.7% change. During this period, the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, which Applied Materials falls in, has lost 10.8%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Applied Materials is expected to post earnings of $4.06 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +87.1%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $12.79 points to a change of +35.8% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $18.28 indicates a change of +42.9% from what Applied Materials is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -0.1%.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Applied Materials.

Story Continues

12 Month EPS

Revenue Growth Forecast

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

In the case of Applied Materials, the consensus sales estimate of $10.3 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +51.4%. The $34.25 billion and $45.65 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +20.7% and +33.3%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Applied Materials reported revenues of $9.12 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +24.8%. EPS of $3.5 for the same period compares with $2.48 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +1.31%. The EPS surprise was +3.55%.

The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Applied Materials is graded D on this front, indicating that it is trading at a premium to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Conclusion

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Applied Materials. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

news.Title: Intel Surpasses Q3 Earnings Estimates on Robust Data Center Demand
news.Content:
Intel Corporation INTC reported solid third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings and revenues beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Strong demand for server processors, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, supported top-line growth despite weakness in the PC market.

Non-GAAP earnings surged 126.1% year over year to 52 cents per share, surpassing the consensus estimate of 39 cents by 33.33%. Revenues increased 20.9% to $16.51 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion by 0.44%. Data Center and AI revenues jumped 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise and neo-cloud customers. However, a soft fourth-quarter outlook overshadowed the feel-good factor for investors and shares plunged more than 25% in pre-market trading.

Intel Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Intel Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Intel Corporation Quote

Data Center Business Drives Growth

Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenues increased to $7.32 billion from $4.12 billion in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, revenues improved 17%, supported by higher server CPU output and robust demand for AI infrastructure. Purpose-built silicon revenues increased more than 50% sequentially and more than doubled year over year.

DCAI operating income rose to $3.04 billion from $964 million a year ago, with operating margin expanding to 41.5% from 23.4%. Higher revenues and lower operating expenses aided profitability. Granite Rapids became the largest product family in Intel's server portfolio, while Clearwater Forest began generating revenues. Management highlighted strong customer interest in Diamond Rapids and the new Intel GPU D-series for AI workloads.

Client Business Faces Memory Shortages

Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) revenues declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion from $8.54 billion. Revenues fell 9% sequentially as industry-wide memory shortages, higher component prices and constrained IT budgets weakened PC demand. Customers also reduced purchases to manage inventories amid softer consumption.

Despite these headwinds, AI PC revenues grew 35% year over year. Wildcat Lake processor shipments increased approximately 70% sequentially, with available supply sold out. CCPG operating income declined to $2.29 billion from $2.69 billion, while operating margin contracted to 28.2% from 31.6%. Management expects challenging PC market conditions to persist until memory availability and pricing normalize.

Story Continues

Foundry Operations Show Improvement

Intel Foundry revenues climbed 58% year over year to $6.7 billion from $4.24 billion, driven by higher manufacturing volumes and improving execution. Sequential revenues increased 16%, supported by better-than-expected growth in Intel 3 and Intel 18A production. External foundry revenues were $411 million, increasing $118 million sequentially, primarily due to a non-recurring customer program.

The segment reported an operating loss of $1.85 billion compared with a loss of $2.32 billion a year ago. Improved manufacturing yields, shorter production cycles and higher factory utilization helped reduce wafer costs. Intel 18A manufacturing costs declined approximately 40% since the first quarter. The company also released its Intel 14A process design kit in October, advancing its next-generation manufacturing roadmap.

Operating Margins Expand

Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 44.1% from 40% a year ago, reflecting a more favorable product mix and lower manufacturing costs. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 19.6% from 11.2%, supported by higher revenues and disciplined spending.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $3.23 billion from $1.52 billion, while adjusted net income attributable to Intel rose to $2.76 billion from $1.02 billion. Non-GAAP research and development and marketing, general and administrative expenses increased to $4.05 billion from $3.93 billion. On a GAAP basis, net income attributable to Intel declined to $3.32 billion from $4.06 billion.

Cash Position Strengthens

Intel generated $5.08 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter compared with $2.55 billion a year ago. Adjusted free cash flow improved to $1.64 billion from $896 million, despite continued investments in manufacturing capacity and advanced process technologies.

As of Sept. 26, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $21.85 billion, while short-term investments totaled $32.16 billion. Long-term debt was $46.32 billion. The company completed a $23 billion equity offering in August, strengthening its financial flexibility to fund capacity expansion and address growing server demand.

Soft Fourth-Quarter Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Intel expects revenues between $15 billion and $16 billion. At the midpoint, non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 38%, with adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share. GAAP earnings are expected to be 10 cents per share.

Management expects DCAI revenues to increase by a mid-teens percentage sequentially, while CCPG revenues are projected to decline more than 20%. Guidance incorporates an estimated $300 million revenue impact from a manufacturing disruption at its Israel facility. Intel expects 2026 gross capital expenditures of $20 billion, with spending projected to increase significantly in 2027 to support expanding production capacity.

Zacks Rank

Intel currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Upcoming Releases

Arista Networks Inc. ANET is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 earnings on Nov. 3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $1.08 per share, suggesting growth of 44% from the year-ago reported figure.

Arista has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 22.8%. Arista delivered an average earnings surprise of 8.9% in the last four reported quarters.

Akamai has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 5.9%. Akamai delivered an average earnings surprise of 4.8% in the last four reported quarters.

GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. GFS is set to release third-quarter 2026 earnings on Nov. 4. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at 51 cents per share, implying a rise of 24.4% from the year-ago reported figure.

news.Title: Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Analysis
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . A Closer Look at the Upcoming Payout, Dividend History, and Growth Outlook for the Semiconductor Leader Texas Instruments Inc ( NASDAQ:TXN ) recently announced a total dividend of $1.52 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-10-30. This amount consists of a $1.52 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-11-10. For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a key marker: shareholders must own the stock before that date to qualify for the payment. As investors look forward to this upcoming distribution, the spotlight also shines on the company's dividend history, yield, and growth rates. Using data from GuruFocus, let's look into Texas Instruments Inc's dividend performance and assess its sustainability. What Does Texas Instruments Inc Do? Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with TXN. High Yield Dividend Stocks in Gurus' Portfolio This Powerful Chart Made Peter Lynch 29% A Year For 13 Years How to calculate the intrinsic value of a stock? Is TXN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Texas Instruments designs and manufactures semiconductors sold to electronics designers and manufacturers worldwide, generating $17.68 billion of revenue in 2025. Its Analog segment (about 79% of revenue) supplies power management and signal chain chips that condition, amplify, convert, and manage electrical signals and power in nearly every type of electronic equipment; its Embedded Processing segment provides microcontrollers and processors. TI's portfolio exceeds 80,000 products serving industrial, automotive, personal electronics, data center, and communications markets, sold largely through its own direct channel. Its competitive advantages include internal manufacturing and technology, highlighted by a multi-year investment cycle in 300-millimeter wafer fabs in Texas and Utah, portfolio breadth, channel reach, and product longevity. Founded in 1930 and headquartered in Dallas, TI manages the business to maximize long-term free cash flow per share. A Glimpse at Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend History Texas Instruments Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 1985, and dividends are currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2001. The stock is thus listed as a dividend aristocrat, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 25 years. For value investors, such a long record signals disciplined capital allocation and a management team committed to returning cash to shareholders through complete business cycles. Story Continues Below is a chart showing annual Dividends Per Share for tracking historical trends. Breaking Down Texas Instruments Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth As of today, Texas Instruments Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.92% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 2.04%. The gap between the two suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. The trailing yield reflects dividends actually paid over the past year, while the forward yield incorporates the most recent dividend rate annualized, so a higher forward figure implies the payout has recently been raised. Over the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 5.50%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate increased to 8.00% per year. And over the past decade, Texas Instruments Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 15.20%. This pattern of decelerating growth from the 10-year to the 3-year window is worth noting: it may reflect a more mature payout policy or a period of heavier capital investment in manufacturing capacity. Based on Texas Instruments Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Texas Instruments Inc stock as of today is approximately 2.82%. Yield on cost estimates the effective return on today's investment after five years of assumed dividend growth, offering a forward-looking complement to the current yield. The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-09-30, Texas Instruments Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.73. And this may suggest that the company's dividend may not be sustainable, since a ratio approaching three-quarters of earnings leaves a narrower cushion for reinvestment and adverse conditions. Texas Instruments Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Texas Instruments Inc's profitability 8 out of 10 as of 2026-09-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported positive net income for each year over the past decade, further solidifying its high profitability. This earnings consistency is an important counterweight when judging whether the current payout level can be maintained. Growth Metrics: The Future Outlook To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Texas Instruments Inc's growth rank of 8 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. However, the headline rank should be read alongside the underlying operating trends discussed below, which have been uneven in recent years amid a cyclical semiconductor downturn and heavy capital spending. Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Texas Instruments Inc's revenue per share , combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate , indicates a strong revenue model. Texas Instruments Inc's revenue has increased by approximately -3.60% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 63.15% of global competitors. The negative figure reflects the recent industry correction rather than a structural loss of demand, but it does temper the growth picture. The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Texas Instruments Inc's earnings increased by approximately -16.80% per year on average, a rate that underperforms approximately 67.5% of global competitors. Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of -6.00% underperforms approximately 69.47% of global competitors. Next Steps for Dividend-Focused Investors Texas Instruments Inc's dividend story is one of strong foundations and near-term tension. On the positive side, the company has paid dividends since 1985, raised them every year since 2001, and holds dividend aristocrat status, backed by a profitability rank of 8 out of 10 and a decade of positive net income. The forward yield of 2.04% exceeding the trailing 1.92% points to continued increases, and a 5-year yield on cost of roughly 2.82% rewards patient holders. Yet a payout ratio of 0.73, combined with negative three-year revenue and EPS growth and a -6.00% five-year EBITDA trend, suggests the dividend consumes a meaningful share of earnings during the current downturn. For value investors, the key question is whether Texas Instruments Inc's long-term free cash flow per share can resume growth as analog demand recovers and the 300-millimeter fab investment cycle matures. A payout ratio near 0.73 is not alarming for a cyclical semiconductor leader, but it warrants monitoring alongside cash flow rather than earnings alone. Readers should watch upcoming quarterly reports for signs of revenue stabilization and capital spending discipline. The integration of HomeBuddy, which expanded QuinStreet's capacity to serve clients, had also progressed well. Continued benefits from this acquisition are likely to have helped the company increase revenues and improve profitability in the to-be-reported quarter.

QuinStreet is working to improve operating efficiency through artificial intelligence (AI) applications, greater use of owned and operated media and a shift toward higher-margin products. The company previously stated positive results from its AI initiatives. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 11.1% from 8.4% in the prior-year quarter. news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周五(30日)齊步收低，上證指數( SSEC )連2日收黑，失守3600點大關，本周跌2.48%，周線連六跌，月線累跌逾6%，創業板指與科創50指數月線均跌逾23%，深證成指( SZI )也連六周報跌，本周收黑7.2%，月線收低15.94%。

滬指周五收低1.44%至3599.02點，深指收跌2.73%至10833.78點，創業板指收黑4.13%至2413.63點，科創50指數重挫5.48%，全市場成交額1兆6744億元(人民幣，下同)，較上一日放量1179億元。

盤面上，光通訊族群領跌兩市，科瑞思、燦勤科技、會暢科技、德科立、移遠通信等跌停或跌超10%，太辰光、新易盛、勝宏科技均跌超13%；影視院線類股亦重挫，文投控股、橫店影視、慈文傳媒、奧飛娛樂、捷成股份觸及跌停；軟體、半導體、軍工類族群亦跌幅居前，通達海、指南針、道通科技、財富趨勢、華大九天、三維天地等逾20股跌停或跌超10%。

上漲族群方面，白酒族群全天強勢表現，黑芝麻、瀘州老窖、新乳業、皇台酒業、古井貢酒、迎駕貢酒、青島食品、好想你等股漲停；港口航運股掀漲停潮，錦江航運、中遠航運等漲停；銀行族群續揚，西安銀行暴漲8.64%，青農商行大漲5.57%，蘇州銀行、長沙銀行等漲超2%。

根據Wind統計數據，滬深兩市及北交所共893檔股票上漲，4598檔下跌，平盤82檔。另據大智慧VIP，滬深北三市共61檔股票漲幅在9%以上，266檔股票跌幅在9%以上。

東海證券表示，滬指收復5日線後再失守，量能略放，大單資金未能延續淨流入，而是大幅淨流出超256億元，日線KDJ尚未死叉，日線MACD尚未黃金交叉，日線指標延續矛盾。指數再度趨近下方555日均線支撐，與120周均線3618點也是一步之遙。目前指數日線技術條件尚未明顯向好，分鐘線指標再度走弱。目前指數上有5週、10週均線壓力，下有120週均線支撐，短線或呈區間震盪態勢。

中原證券認為，當前滬指與創業板指數的平均本益比分別為16.14倍、37.37倍，處於近三年中位數平均上方，適合中長期佈局。中國國家統計局數據顯示，今年前三季GDP年增4.6%，高技術製造業占規模以上工業增加值的比重同比提升1.6個百分點，新動能對經濟成長貢獻率保持在40%以上，滬指繼續震盪整理的機率較大，結構再平衡為核心特徵，宜密切關注宏觀經濟數據、海外流動性變化以及政策動向，短線建議關注航天裝備、軍工電子、風電設備及銀行等產業的投資機會。

萬聯證券亦稱，從經濟數據看，國民經濟運行平穩，宏觀調控維持適度寬鬆的基調。資本市場方面，10月A股流動性指標表現分化，市場投資者情緒與風險偏好受多因素影響，市場改善仍需更多支持。隨著相關部門持續深化資本市場投融資綜合改革，擴大耐心資本、長期資本和戰略資本供給，預計市場韌性有望增強，流動性環境有望改善。多重利多政策提振下，市場信心有望修復。從業績看，今年第三季財報披露接近尾聲，結構性亮點湧現。一方面，新質生產力領域，在技術創新與產業鏈協同帶動下保持高景氣增長。另一方面，具備技術、成本與供應鏈優勢的出海龍頭企業展現出較強的盈利韌性。

news.Title: SanDisk Corp (SNDK) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Highlights: Revenue Surges 378% as Data Center Demand ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Revenue of $11 billion exceeded guidance, up 23% sequentially and 378% year-over-year, driven by strong demand and pricing.

Non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%, above guidance, and non-GAAP EPS was $49.51, significantly beating the $44-$46 range.

Data center revenue grew 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, with three U.S. hyperscalers as customers, and is expected to represent over 55% of the market in 2027.

New business model (NBM) partnerships provide long-term demand visibility, with 50% of bits under NBM for fiscal 2027 and two-thirds for fiscal 2028, and a pipeline exceeding supply through 2030.

Generated $5.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow (52% margin) and returned $5 billion to shareholders through buybacks, with no debt and $5.1 billion in cash.

Negative Points

Consumer revenue declined 29% sequentially to $397 million as the market adjusts to higher pricing.

Edge revenue growth was only 7% sequentially, with contraction at the lower end partially offsetting resilience in premium and mainstream markets.

PC and smartphone unit volumes are declining, with PC units down this year and expected to be slightly down next year, impacting near-term demand.

Fiscal Q3 is historically the weakest sequential quarter, and management advised conservatism for sequential growth from Q2 to Q3.

HBF and other new NAND technologies are still in early stages, with no revenue contribution included in the long-term financial model, and timing of meaningful revenue remains uncertain.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Can you elaborate on the NBM pipeline exceeding supply through the end of the decade, and how is that changing your thought process around bit supply and CapEx plans? A : CEO David Goeckeler said the process is working, with a robust pipeline now extending through 2030 and beyond as customers offer demand signals and financial commitments. He noted these agreements could eventually inform supply decisions, but negotiations and commitments are still underway. CFO Luis Visoso added that gross CapEx is expected at a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue for fiscal 2027.

Q : You signed two NBMs before the last call. Should we expect many more, and what percentage of bits is under contract for the next few years? A : Goeckeler said the NBM pipeline is very strong and growing, and it has become the predominant way SanDisk deals with customers. About 50% of bits are under NBM for fiscal 2027 and about two-thirds for fiscal 2028, with that percentage expected to rise. Visoso noted 95% of NBM partners are investment grade and generated about $130 billion in operating cash flow.

Story Continues

Q : Data center revenue is up almost 20x year-over-year and 61% sequentially. What is driving that penetration, and will data center reach half of your own mix? A : Goeckeler credited the BiCS8 node and CBA architecture, the right TLC and QLC products at the right time, and more refined AI inference architectures. He said customers are increasingly using TLC, QLC, and even SLC in different parts of the architecture. He added SanDisk is working to catch up to the market's data center bit mix and expects a substantially higher mix than in fiscal 2026.

Q : In fiscal Q1, about 60% of revenue growth came from volume and 40% from pricing. How do you expect that mix to progress in guidance? A : Visoso said both volume and pricing are expected to contribute in the next quarter, with modest like-for-like price increases. He added pricing is expected to continue increasing modestly throughout the year.

Q : Can you provide more detail on HBF progress and customer discussions, and how do you view new NAND tiers such as StorageNext and CMX context memory? A : Goeckeler said HBF customer conversations are robust and ongoing, with samples expected to reach customers next calendar year. He described the proliferation of new NAND tiers as healthy, saying AI inference architectures are being relentlessly refined for economics, which is pulling NAND into more parts of the architecture. He said SanDisk is staying close to the customers spending money to scale infrastructure.

Q : Are you looking to accelerate the BiCS transition from 8 to 9 and 10 to accelerate bit growth and satisfy strong customer demand? A : Goeckeler said SanDisk remains committed to its mid-to-high-teens bit growth plan. He noted node transitions require extensive planning, tool purchases, and line setup, and the fab plan is already set for that bit growth. He said there are no plans to change it at this point.

Q : Are there limits to increasingly allocating bits to data center? A : Goeckeler said there are constraints because fabs produce a certain mix of TLC, QLC, and die types, making it a constant fitting exercise to get the right product to the right customer. Visoso added that over the short term it is almost impossible to change allocation because it takes about 120 days to produce a wafer, but there are more degrees of freedom over the longer term.

Q : With PC units under pressure, are you seeing more NBM interest from the PC market? A : Visoso said SanDisk cannot discuss specific customers but has NBMs in data center and edge, and the construct is offered to any customer that wants it. Goeckeler said PC units are down this year and slightly down next year, with the current two calendar quarters representing the trough of year-over-year compares. He expects PC exabytes to grow next year as content per device rises.

Q : How do you see enterprise SSD content per server progressing in 2027 amid agentic AI proliferation? A : Goeckeler said SanDisk sees roughly 60 to 90 gigabytes of NAND demand per CPU in inference and agent orchestration applications. He said more NAND is being pulled into the inference architecture across TLC, QLC, and high-endurance solutions, and SanDisk will continue working on TAM analysis and trade-offs.

Q : Do you have an updated view on enterprise SSD share goals? A : Goeckeler said he has deliberately avoided setting specific share goals because they can lead to perverse portfolio choices. He said SanDisk will clearly mix higher into data center, noting 17x year-over-year growth, and expects that mix to go higher through 2027, but declined to provide a specific target.

Q : What is the prevailing TLC versus QLC mix among CSP customers, and will it shift meaningfully later this decade? A : Goeckeler said the mix remains about 70-30 TLC to QLC and is expected to stay there at least for the rest of the fiscal year. He said customers are discussing a reacceleration of QLC in different use cases, and the QLC product has been very well received with qualifications complete and customers ramping.

Q : Given double-digit mobile unit declines this year, can your mobile bits still grow next year? A : Goeckeler said the low end of the mobile market is under pressure, leading to unit declines, but content per unit is increasing. He expects exabyte growth in that market next year on a slightly declining unit count and said SanDisk will manage its portfolio with agility and balance.

A : Visoso said SanDisk has not seen any credit concerns and demand from customers is strengthening. He said the largest customers are basically all investment grade with strong cash generation. news.Title: Applied Materials vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Comparing Revenue Growth Trends Between These Artificial Intelligence Companies
news.Content:
Applied Materials: A Gradual Revenue Uptrend

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) primarily generates its revenue by designing, developing, and manufacturing the complex wafer fabrication equipment and materials engineering tools used by its diverse base of global customers to produce integrated circuits.

This year, it officially unveiled a large research and development center in California designed specifically for collaborative engineering, and it additionally appointed a new executive to serve on its board of directors.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing: Consistent Revenue Expansion

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE:TSM) primarily earns its revenue by operating as a global dedicated foundry, meaning it manufactures, packages, and meticulously tests complex integrated circuits on behalf of various third-party technology clients around the world.

While operating within a complex international regulatory environment, it announced a collaborative industry initiative to transition to advanced photomasks, and its first Arizona fabrication plant successfully reached production yield rates comparable to its primary facilities in Taiwan.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue serves as the basic top-line indicator of the total capital flowing into a business from its core commercial operations before any operating expenses are deducted. Closely tracking this top-line financial figure helps investors understand the total scale and growth trajectory of a business.

Foolish Take

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, popularly known as TSMC, delivers far greater revenue than Applied Materials despite both providing essential services for the semiconductor industry. That's because TSMC is the world's dominant pure-play semiconductor foundry, controlling over 70% of the market. Applied Materials sells specialized materials engineering, deposition, and etching systems to chipmakers like TSMC.

Thanks to the artificial intelligence boom, TSMC is experiencing historic demand for its manufacturing prowess. The same tailwind is helping Applied Materials this year, as sales have taken off. Its rapid revenue growth in recent quarters was marked by the highest quarter-over-quarter revenue growth in company history during its fiscal third quarter, ended July 26.

Applied Materials was able to achieve this due to diligent planning and foresight. It nearly doubled its total manufacturing footprint over the past several years, capped off by opening a state-of-the-art manufacturing center in Singapore during Q3. This enabled the company to build and ship equipment at an unprecedented rate to fuel the global AI infrastructure surge.

news.Title: The Case Against a SpaceX and Tesla Merger
news.Content:
While we don't know what terms, if any, are on the table for a potential merger, there's a strong case that now isn't the best time for Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to pursue a merger with Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX). The argument rests on two main ideas. First, it runs contrary to market trends; second, Tesla is on the cusp of delivering significant shareholder value after years of disappointment.

Different risk and capital profiles

Over the last decade, the major trend with industrial conglomerates such as General Electric, United Technologies Corporation, Honeywell , 3M , Danaher , Johnson Controls , and Emerson Electric has been to break them up. While each company had its own circumstances, three themes apply to all:

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Separating companies allows for greater management and operational focus.

The market has tended to apply a so-called conglomerate discount, and investors increasingly value the ability to make targeted investments.

Each company has its own specific risk and its own capital allocation priorities, and they are better served as stand-alone companies.

Given the incredible complexity inherent in managing Tesla (EVs, robotaxi/Cybercab, Optimus, energy generation/storage, charging infrastructure, and a host of investments in building its own supply chain) and SpaceX (launch services, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, Starlink, defense networks), it's not hard to see how complex a merged entity would become.

The argument over the conglomerate discount is admittedly subject to change, as conglomerates once commanded a premium. However, that's not the case now, and until it changes, there's no strong reason to believe a merger will lead to an immediate market-valuation rerating of the merged entity. On the contrary, the opposite could occur.

Different risk profiles and capital profiles

The argument from specific risk and capital profiles is the strongest. Tesla is on the cusp of beginning a multiyear journey to scale its robotaxi service and generate a long stream of recurring revenue from robotaxi/Cybercab. Investors can disagree on its profit potential amid competition, but robotaxi/Cybercab is baked into the valuation, and if you are holding the stock, you presumably believe in the potential of autonomous driving.

Story Continues

While it will obviously require significant upfront capital investment to build out the network, Tesla has the resources to do so and create a company with significant long-term cash flows. The same argument, albeit a few more years out, applies to Optimus. Tesla does not need SpaceX to achieve its own goals.

In contrast, SpaceX operates in a high-risk sector that requires even more massive capital investment. Moreover, while Starlink is currently SpaceX's profit generator, its revenue driver is the Super Intelligence business. The former is effectively funding growth in the latter.

Tesla is moving toward becoming a company with a long-term stream of recurring revenue, scaling robotaxi/Cybercab and, in time, Optimus, and a play on physical AI. In contrast, SpaceX is a business that requires massive, ongoing, and uncertain capital expenditures and is a play on AI infrastructure.

Regarding the uncertainty of capital expenditures, consider orbital data centers and SpaceX. Their depreciation rate is likely to be high because they realistically can't be serviced in space and, unlike terrestrial data centers, which can replace servers and chips, will likely last only as long as their graphics processing units (GPUs) remain useful. A high depreciation rate implies higher maintenance capital spending.

Tesla hasn't released value from robotaxi/Cybercab yet

To understand this argument, consider how private equity might run Tesla. Their typical model is to generate value from the investment and sell the asset only once the business is firing on all cylinders, and it can optimize the price.

If you believe Tesla will evolve into a company generating billions of recurring revenue from its Cybercab fleet and then from Optimus, it makes sense to hold the asset, at least until the company proves the doubters wrong and releases value from the robotaxi rollout. At which point, Tesla shareholders will be in a stronger position to demand a healthier premium for the business.

What it means to investors

Again, while it's true that we don't know what kind of offer or what deal it will be, or even if there will be a proposal at all, the reality is the value of Tesla will key off of its current market price, and if you think it's undervalued and/or want to wait until the company releases value from robotaxi, then an offer now is unlikely to lead to a favorable outcome for you.

All told, in a merger, Tesla investors would dilute their claim on cash flows from robotaxi, EVs, and robotics (physical AI) in favor of using that cash to support space exploration and cloud computing (AI infrastructure). This creates a merged company with a significantly different risk and capital-allocation profile from Tesla, and they might not get full value for their Tesla shares until robotaxi scales.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

Positive Points

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) exceeded $1 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, with Q3 revenue of $1.2 billion, up 22% sequentially and 63% year-over-year.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) expanded capacity to support over $6 billion in annual revenue and expects $8 billion by the second half of 2027, with a path to $10 billion.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) raised its enterprise data growth floor to 150% year-over-year, driven by customer diversification, module adoption, and content gains.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) achieved its first large data converter design win, expected to ramp next year, and continues to increase its SAM with high-speed memory products.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) repurchased over $450 million of its own stock in Q3, reflecting confidence in its growth trajectory.

Negative Points

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) expects notebook strength to be limited in the short term due to memory constraints, with segment growth roughly flat to up slightly year-over-year.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) does not expect 800-volt GaN revenue until late 2027 or 2028, and the technology requires shipping about 50 million units to prove reliability.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) is absorbing some cost increases and not raising prices, which could pressure margins if costs continue to rise.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) faces competitive risk from integrated voltage regulators and industry consolidation, such as Analog Devices' acquisition of Empower.

Monolithic Power Systems Inc ( NASDAQ:MPWR ) noted that its building automation opportunity, though large, will take time to materialize and the path to $50 billion revenue is still unclear.

Story Continues

Q & A Highlights

Q : Tore Svanberg of Stifel asked for elaboration on the "accelerated growth" commentary and when the $10 billion capacity target might be in place, given the company is on track to grow 50%-60% this year. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the company sees an "explosive growth period in the next few years" with no signs of slowing down. CFO Tony Balow added that growth is broadening across multiple end markets, including auto (ramping since Q2) and robotics, giving confidence that growth will continue beyond existing businesses.

Q : Quinn Bolton of Needham asked whether the company could raise its floor for enterprise data growth and offer thoughts on 2027. A : CFO Tony Balow said that given Q3 results and Q4 guidance, the company is comfortable raising its enterprise data growth floor to 150% year over year, up from 130%. He said it is too early to put a percentage on 2027, but all growth drivers remain intact, including customer diversification, module growth, and content gains, with Agentic AI workloads potentially an added tailwind.

Q : Rick Schafer of Oppenheimer asked about the storage and compute segment, including the split between DDR5, HDD, SSD, and PC vCore power, given PC units tracking down about 20% in the second half. A : CFO Tony Balow said DDR5 PMIC solutions are the biggest growth driver, with healthy growth also in HDD and SSD storage. Notebook strength is weaker due to downstream memory constraints, but he remains bullish long-term given good technology and share. He characterized the segment overall as roughly flattish to up a couple of points year over year, "a tale of two cities" with strong storage offset by a limited notebook TAM.

Q : Rick Schafer of Oppenheimer asked how the new CFO views OpEx growth and whether the company could see material operating leverage at 50%-60% top-line growth. A : CEO Michael Hsing said he never believed big R&D dollars equate to bigger results, calling it "inversely proportional" and emphasizing good ideas and people. CFO Tony Balow said the model won't change, but at current growth rates the company will fall below its OpEx model range because it simply cannot spend money that fast.

Q : Will Stein of Truist asked about gross margin, specifically whether the company could exceed its historical 10-20 basis points per quarter expansion given the growth. A : CFO Tony Balow said Q3 gross margin rose 10 basis points and Q4 guidance implies another 10 basis points, keeping the company squarely in its 55%-60% sweet spot with slow, methodical expansion. CEO Michael Hsing added that during capacity constraints the company does not gouge customers, aiming for consistent performance year over year.

Q : Chris Caso of Wolfe Research asked how the company is dealing with rising costs, including higher wafer prices, and whether it is passing costs along to customers. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the company absorbs some cost increases, does not raise prices, and shares cost increases with customers, noting customers "have a very long memory." CFO Tony Balow added that pricing is not a significant contributor to revenue growth; the focus is on not diluting gross margin.

Q : Tore Svanberg of Stifel asked for more detail on the 800-volt GaN product sampling, including the technology type and timing of revenue. A : CEO Michael Hsing said the GaN solution is based on in-house development, following earlier silicon carbide work, and customers can choose between GaN and SiC. He stressed caution on reliability, targeting below 1 ppm failures and wanting to ship roughly 50 million GaN units before declaring it proven. CFO Tony Balow said 800-volt architecture ramps are expected in late 2027 with more in 2028.

Q : Joshua Buchalter of TD Cowen asked about the diversity of the enterprise data business, including GPU versus ASIC and modules versus discrete. A : CEO Michael Hsing said modules are increasingly used because of high power demand across server applications. CFO Tony Balow said since mid-2025 there has been rapid growth in ASIC customers, primarily using modules with higher ASPs, and that AI-driven design tools will let the company address a longer tail of smaller customers that may become large ones.

Q : Sebastien Naji of William Blair asked about integrated voltage regulators and Analog Devices' acquisition of Empower, and whether MPS sees competitive risk in AI data centers. A : CEO Michael Hsing dismissed much of the discussion as "BS talks," saying MPS has its own solutions and can deliver whatever customers want. He noted GPU power levels and power delivery architectures evolve quickly, and the company does not discuss products until it clearly sees where revenue will come from.

Q : Kelsey Chia of Citi asked about the switching business, its contribution to communications growth, the 2027 ramp, and whether it is accretive to gross margins. A : CFO Tony Balow said switching is likely the fastest-growing sub-end market within communications on a percentage basis, though from a small base, and optical modules should remain a significant growth driver into 2027. On margins, he said all end markets operate around the corporate average, so growth in any one market should not take the company out of its 55%-60% model.

Q : Joe Quatrochi of Wells Fargo asked about working capital and go-to-market investments needed to support the expansion to $8 billion in capacity. A : CFO Tony Balow said the fabless model means the company does not have to "dig a hole and pour concrete," so he does not anticipate a large increase in capital intensity to support the capacity expansion, nor a change to the capital structure.

Q : Gary Mobley of StoneX asked whether the $8 billion capacity target exiting fiscal 2027 signals revenue velocity, and about inventory levels. A : CFO Tony Balow said the company is signaling that capacity will stay ahead of the business, as it has for 20 years, and that it sees demand coming, though it is too early to map capacity to a 2027 quarterly revenue ramp. On inventory, he said channel inventory remains at the lean end of the normal 5-8 week range and internal inventory is not limiting the business.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Story Continues

Release Date: October 29, 2026

Positive Points

Record quarterly revenue of $1.006 billion, up 25% year-over-year, with broad-based growth across both segments and geographies.

Adjusted gross margin reached 48.9%, the highest in over 25 years, expanding 530 basis points year-over-year despite investments and higher compensation.

Strong demand environment with book-to-bill significantly above one, backlog up more than 35% sequentially and more than doubling year-over-year.

Adjusted EBITDA margin exceeded 30% and is expected to reach ~31% in Q4, demonstrating strong operating leverage with EBITDA growth outpacing revenue growth.

Record operating and free cash flow of $224 million, enabling early repayment of the 2029 term loan and reducing net leverage to 2.9x, with further improvement expected.

Negative Points

Q1 2027 revenue is expected to decline mid-single-digit percentage sequentially due to seasonality and fewer selling days, despite year-over-year growth.

KSP facility remains dilutive to gross margins through most of 2027, and Colorado facility will be dilutive for about a year behind KSP, impacting near-term profitability.

Mainstream utilization remains the most underutilized part of the market, with memory tightness potentially capping near-term growth in mainstream applications.

Supply chain pinch points exist, notably in CMP pads where capacity is constrained, requiring selective CapEx to unlock.

No material pricing benefits were included in Q3 or Q4 guidance, and pricing actions are limited to new orders, not backlog, limiting near-term margin upside from pricing.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Melissa Weathers of Deutsche Bank asked what drove the upside in the quarter versus guidance incremental supply coming online or strengthening demand? A : CEO David Reeder attributed the revenue beat primarily to execution: demand was strong, and the team increased production and throughput beyond expectations, converting more backlog into revenue. Strength was broad-based, particularly in CapEx-related businesses. CFO Sukhi Nagesh added that the higher sales volume drove roughly 130 basis points of sequential gross margin expansion through factory absorption, yield initiatives, and lower inventory, scrap, and rework despite higher incentive compensation and labor investment.

Q : Melissa Weathers asked for initial thoughts on 2027, including MSI and CapEx growth. A : CEO David Reeder said the industry setup is "incredibly constructive" across all major demand drivers, with momentum exiting 2026 expected to extend well into 2027. Industry forecasts call for MSI growth broadly consistent with 2026, and all indications point to another strong double-digit growth year for both WFE and fab construction. More detail will come at the November 9 Capital Markets Day.

Q : Elizabeth Sun of Citi asked whether the strong growth can continue into next year given the growing backlog, and whether suppliers can keep up. A : CEO David Reeder said the lion's share of momentum is company performance rather than market-driven, with initiatives launched in late 2025 bearing fruit in 2026. He reiterated that Entegris has significantly more than $1 billion of incremental capacity in its network to support 2027 demand and beyond. The company is working closely with customers to validate demand and cascade it into the supply chain; some pinch points are inevitable but are being proactively identified and addressed.

Q : Aleksey Yefremov of Barclays asked about strong incremental margins and whether they are sustainable given investment needs, plus differences between segments. A : CFO Sukhi Nagesh said incremental gross margin of close to 60% and incremental EBITDA margin above 40% are in line with targets, driven largely by self-help execution productivity, yield, inventory and scrap control. He expects the trend to continue into next year. CEO David Reeder added that most of the sequential increase came from Entegris' ability to satisfy demand already in front of it, weighted somewhat toward CapEx-related revenue, with more unit pull than originally expected.

Q : Timothy Arcuri of UBS asked for a preview of the growth-versus-market rubric (historically 4 to 6 points of outgrowth) ahead of Capital Markets Day. A : CEO David Reeder said the framework will be "somewhat consistent" with what Entegris has articulated in the past, deferring fuller detail to the November 9 Capital Markets Day.

Q : Timothy Arcuri asked about the margin impact from the Colorado and KSP facilities and what clean gross margin would look like without the dilution. A : CFO Sukhi Nagesh said KSP reached gross profit breakeven in Q3, a big accomplishment, with an exciting ramp expected in Q4 and 2027. The Colorado facility is operational and producing samples, with revenue expected to begin next year roughly a 12-month lag behind KSP South. CEO David Reeder added that KSP remains dilutive to enterprise gross margins through most of 2027, becoming roughly neutral as the company exits 2027, with Colorado about a year behind; current results are fully burdened by both facilities.

Q : James Schneider of Goldman Sachs asked whether Entegris has enough capacity for revenue growth over the next couple of years given ramps in Colorado and KSP, and whether it is rethinking manufacturing footprint optimization. A : CEO David Reeder said Entegris has run the demand profile against internal capacity models and feels good about 2027 and 2028, with substantial capacity left to unlock through network optimization, centralized procurement, yield, and productivity. The company will selectively spend CapEx to relieve pinch points.

Q : Chris Parkinson of Wolfe Research asked about momentum and share position in MS and CMP, including slurries and pads, across geographies. A : CEO David Reeder noted broad geographic strength in Q3 North America up 22%, Taiwan up 41%, Southeast Asia up 51%, and Japan up 29% year over year. MS has accelerated through the year from low single-digit growth to the mid-to-high single digits and now squarely into the teens, anchored by CMP. He feels very good about slurries; pads are the one area where capacity is a small pinch point being unlocked as quickly as possible.

Q : Charles Shi of Needham questioned the guidance for a mid-single-digit sequential revenue decline in Q1 2027, which is steeper than normal seasonality. Underlying momentum, orders, and customer feedback remain strong. CEO David Reeder noted Entegris formally guides only one quarter at a time and was providing early color on Q1.

He flagged mainstream logic utilization about 55% of MSI as the key wildcard for 2027.

Q : Edward Yang of Oppenheimer asked where the industry sits in the multi-wave demand cycle of fab construction, WFE, and wafer starts, and whether the waves are overlapping. news.Title: 陸股慘變熊市、資金湧向債市，30年期國債ETF10月淨流入138億人民幣
news.Content:
【財訊快報／劉敏夫】外電報導指出，隨著中國股市持續下跌，中國投資者湧入追蹤長期國債的交易所交易基金(ETF)，在上漲的債市中尋求避險。根據金融媒體匯編的數據顯示，兩支與30年期國債掛鉤的境內ETF在10月淨流入資金138億元人民幣(21億美元)，創2025年7月以來最高水準。

這波資金流入已推動兩支基金的市值均創下歷史新高。金融媒體匯編的數據顯示，自下半年開始以來，鵬揚中債-30年期國債ETF已上漲57%，博時上證30年期國債ETF上漲68%。

國債受到多重因素支撐，包括經濟成長溫和、充裕的流動性、以及對本地投資者有吸引力的其他投資選擇缺乏。中國股市表現低迷，10月跌入熊市，主要受消費持續不振以及有關AI盈利能力的質疑拖累。

華源證券固收首席分析師廖志明在本週的報告中表示，投資者尤其青睞期限較長的債券，這類債券在第四季度還有進一步上漲的空間。他預計，降低借貸成本以及債券供應減少將推動30年期國債殖利率在年底前邁向2%，目前在2.05%左右。

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Revenue: $560 million, up 24% sequentially and 131% year-over-year; fourth consecutive record quarter, above guidance of $519M$541M.

Gross Margin: 53.7%, significantly above guidance on favorable product mix and better-than-expected Ferri automotive margins.

Operating Expenses: $120.7 million, slightly down sequentially.

Release Date: October 29, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Silicon Motion Technology Corp ( NASDAQ:SIMO ) delivered record Q3 2026 revenue of $560 million, up 24% sequentially and 131% year-over-year, exceeding guidance.

Gross margin reached 53.7%, significantly above guidance, driven by better product mix and higher margins in Ferri automotive products.

Earnings per ADS was $4.35, a 79% sequential increase and 333% year-over-year increase.

The company expects 2026 revenue to more than double year-over-year and projects at least 40% revenue growth in 2027 with gross margins in the low-to-mid 50% range.

Strong momentum in enterprise and automotive segments: MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers on track with all seven announced customers ramping in 2026, and Ferri automotive revenue up over 75% sequentially, representing over 40% of total revenue.

The company secured 2027 wafer supply from TSMC, as well as test and assembly capacity, supporting its growth outlook.

New opportunities in near-CPU boot drives with DRAM, estimated to be a $10 billion market by 2030, with production ramp expected in second-half 2027.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Silicon Motion Technology Corp ( NASDAQ:SIMO ) faces near-term headwinds in its eMMC/UFS controller business due to challenging smartphone OEM demand amid higher NAND and DRAM prices, with revenue expected to remain relatively flat.

The PC and smartphone markets remain weak, with consumer unit volumes declining as OEMs struggle to offer affordable devices amid rising memory and storage costs.

The company expects SSD controller business to be flat to slightly down in Q4 2026 due to current memory and storage environment and typical seasonality.

NAND supply remains tight, and the company anticipates the supply-demand imbalance to persist, with new NAND fabs not planned until 2028.

The arbitration with a key customer (likely Micron) is still pending, creating uncertainty.

The company has limited R&D resources to pursue all opportunities, particularly in the near-CPU boot drive market, which may slow time-to-market.

Working capital needs are increasing, with inventory growing to support growth, though the recent $1.15 billion convertible bond offering provides funding for the next couple of years.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Given the guidance for at least 40% revenue growth next year and gross margin in the low-to-mid 50% range, what are the main drivers? A : CFO Jason Tsai attributed the outlook to significant traction in MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers and aggressive ramping of Ferri automotive solutions, which are multi-year engagements with long product cycles. He noted that based on backlog and anticipated growth from Titan, SSD controllers, and Ferri automotive, the company believes it can sustain low-to-mid 50% gross margins.

Q : Can you discuss the near-CPU boot drive opportunity with DRAM, including the size of the market and the ramp timeline? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that NAND makers are deprioritizing low-capacity near-CPU boot drives (1TB-2TB) as they focus on high-capacity SSDs, creating a significant shortage. He estimates this market will reach at least $10 billion by 2030. Silicon Motion expects firmware and solutions ready by early Q1 2027, with production ramping in the second half of 2027, leveraging its existing controller technology with built-in OCP features.

Q : How is Silicon Motion positioned with wafer supply, packaging, and test capacity to support 40% growth next year, and is there upside potential? A : CEO Wallace Kou acknowledged industry-wide shortages across substrates, materials, wafers, NAND, and test capacity. However, he stated the manufacturing team secured 2027 wafer supply primarily with TSMC, along with test capacity, assembly capacity, and substrate materials. He expressed confidence in supporting at least 40% year-over-year growth, with more detailed 2027 guidance to come next quarter.

Q : As the SSD solution business grows to over 40% of revenue, how do you manage NAND pricing exposure, particularly if NAND prices decline? A : CEO Wallace Kou explained that Silicon Motion negotiates six-month pricing contracts with customers, passing through NAND cost increases while maintaining margin protection. He expects NAND price increases to moderate as spot prices become challenging for module makers. CFO Jason Tsai added that if NAND availability and pricing improve, customers would likely double density, and re-specing to normal specs plus new customer opportunities position the company to grow even as the NAND market stabilizes.

Q : What is the revenue mix between solutions (Ferri, Boot Drive, automotive) and controllers, and how will it change next year? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that approximately 40% of total revenue came from solutions (boot drive, automotive) and 60% from controllers in Q3. He expects the mix to become more balanced at roughly 50/50 next year as automotive solutions grow.

Q : With enterprise and Ferri becoming a larger portion of the business, should we expect consumer seasonality from Q4 to Q1 to diminish? A : CFO Jason Tsai confirmed that as enterprise and Ferri become bigger portions of the mix, normal consumer seasonality will be more muted going forward since the consumer business is becoming a smaller percentage of total revenue. He deferred specific Q1 and 2027 guidance to January.

Q : Can you provide an update on the Singapore arbitration? A : CFO Jason Tsai stated that closing arguments in the Singapore arbitration were held in March, and the company is still awaiting results. He declined to provide additional comments until the outcome is announced.

Q : How should we think about gross margins for the solutions business as NAND prices stabilize, and what working capital is needed to support 50%+ growth in solutions? A : CFO Jason Tsai explained that six-month pricing contracts and tight inventory turns provide margin protection. Automotive products are qualified for multi-year projects (3-5 years) with pricing and supply agreements set at the outset, supporting better margins given the solution complexity and support requirements. Regarding working capital, he stated the $1.15 billion convertible bond raise is sufficient to fund the next couple of years of business based on current forecasts, with inventory growing in Q4 before turning back into cash flow.

Q : What is Silicon Motion's strategy in China regarding NAND makers, CSPs, and competition? A : CEO Wallace Kou emphasized balancing China and the rest of the world, collaborating with YMTC directly and through module makers, and growing local China R&D to support China customers while Taiwan supports U.S. and global customers. He noted that Chinese enterprise controller companies that previously bought NAND at cyclical lows and sold drives at highs are now struggling in a non-cyclical pricing environment. Silicon Motion's strategy is to win NAND maker design wins, hyperscaler customers in both the U.S. and China, and CSPs directly, while selling controllers and firmware through module maker and NAND maker partners.

Q : How do you view the competitive landscape for enterprise controllers in China? A : CEO Wallace Kou stated that while one or two Chinese companies have moved toward IPOs, he does not see them as strong enough to compete long-term on technology or business model. He expressed confidence in Silicon Motion's position, citing its strong development pipeline for PCIe Gen 5 and Gen 6 controllers.

Q : Has the convertible bond issuance changed the dividend policy or capital structure targets? A : CFO Jason Tsai said capital allocation priorities remain unchanged: dividend, opportunistic share buybacks, and M&A as appropriate. The company recently increased its dividend to $2.30 per ADS per year and has a 10-year history of raising it. He noted working capital needs are increasing, and the convertible bond raise puts the company in a better position to drive growth with improved working capital.

Q : What is the outlook for MonTitan demand, particularly regarding HBM/DRAM innovations and KV cache requirements per GPU? A : CEO Wallace Kou said MonTitan demand comes from a wide range of customers including AI server, hyperscalers, CSPs, and the NVIDIA ecosystem. He noted compute SSD demand was larger this year due to high NAND prices, but high-capacity QLC momentum is building for next year as NAND makers ramp 2-terabit QLC production. He expects NVIDIA to redefine minimum KV cache capacity per GPU early next year, and growing KV cache demand will drive additional enterprise SSD and controller demand.

Q : How are you managing OpEx and R&D growth

news.Title: 業績優預期 軸承廠NSK上修財測、純益增5成
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-30 10:54:51 蔡承啟 發佈

AI投資擴大，半導體製造設備用軸承需求穩健，業績優於預期，日本軸承大廠日本精工(NSK)上修今年度財測預估，純益將暴增近5成。不過NSK今日股價未受提振、下挫。

截至日本股市30日早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)為止，NSK下挫2.18%，暫收1,008日圓。

NSK 29日於日股盤後公布財報新聞稿指出，因AI相關投資擴大，帶動半導體製造設備、工具機用產品需求穩健，提振產業機械事業部門(包含工具機、半導體設備用軸承等產品)業績優於預期，加上日圓匯率較預期走貶，因此今年度(2026年度、2026年4月-2027年3月)合併營收目標自原先(7月)預估的1.04兆日圓上修至1.05兆日圓、將年增15.2%，合併營益目標自500億日圓上修至560億日圓、將年增44.3%，合併純益目標自290億日圓上修至340億日圓、將年增48.7%。

日經新聞報導，市場平均預估NSK今年度純益將為341億日圓，NSK上修過後的預估值約略同於市場預期。

NSK並同時公布今年度上半年(2026年4-9月)財報：合併營收較去年同期大增26.2%至5,203.51億日圓、合併營益暴增69.8%至300.66億日圓、合併純益暴增78.8%至188.38億日圓。

4-9月期間NSK產業機械事業部門營收較去年同期成長18.6%至2,144.61億日圓、營益飆增278.4%至184.78億日圓；汽車事業部門(包含車用軸承等產品)營收微減不到0.1%至2,011.36億日圓、營益增加3.0%至91.27億日圓。

news.Title: Sandisk Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Sandisk Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Sandisk reported exceptional fiscal Q1 2027 results , with revenue of $11 billion, up 23% sequentially and 378% year over year. Non-GAAP gross margin was 85.1%, adjusted free cash flow reached $5.7 billion, and the company repurchased $5 billion of stock.

Data-center demand is driving growth : revenue rose 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion as AI workloads increased NAND usage for inference, KV caches, data staging, and data lakes. Sandisk expects data-center demand to remain the industry's primary growth engine in 2027.

Sandisk forecast fiscal Q2 revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and expects continued benefits from long-term customer agreements, with roughly half of fiscal 2027 bits already covered. The company also approved an eight-for-one stock split and plans to begin split-adjusted trading on Nov. 20.

Why Western Digital's AI Storage Boom Defies the Chip Sell-Off

Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 results above its guidance, citing continued demand from AI infrastructure customers, expanding data-center sales and growth in its long-term customer partnership model.

Revenue totaled $11 billion, up 23% sequentially and 378% from the prior-year period. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%, while non-GAAP earnings per share were $49.51. The company generated $5.7 billion in adjusted free cash flow and repurchased $5 billion of stock during the quarter.

→ Apple's Foldable iPhone Sold Out in Minutes, But Wall Street Has Questions

The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer David Goeckeler said the results reflected the company's technology roadmap, customer relationships and financial discipline. "Our strategy is working, and our execution is delivering strong results," he said.

Data center drives growth

Data-center revenue was $4.8 billion, rising 61% sequentially, as Sandisk allocated more supply to the segment. CFO Luis Visoso said the company's products and partnerships with three U.S. hyperscalers supported its expansion in the market.

→ Off-Price, High-Yield: Why Ross Stores Is Defying the Retail Slump

Why Wall Street Expects Even More From SanDisk After Its 575% Rally

Goeckeler said data-center demand has been supported by increasing NAND use across AI inference systems, including applications involving key-value, or KV, caches, data staging and data lakes. Sandisk estimates that data center now represents roughly half of industry NAND bits, compared with approximately 20% early in the decade.

Story Continues

The company expects AI data-center flash demand to expand as inference workloads require greater storage capacity for longer prompts, more complex reasoning, multimodal inputs and persistent user context. Sandisk expects KV cache to represent approximately one-third of the AI data-center flash market by the end of the decade.

→ Coca-Cola Stock Is Everything AI Isn't—And That's Its Biggest Strength

Goeckeler said the company is seeing wider use of both TLC and QLC NAND in AI architectures. In addition, customers are exploring use of NAND configured in SLC mode for applications requiring greater endurance. He characterized those discussions as early-stage but said the trend could expand NAND's addressable market rather than cannibalize other flash products.

Sandisk said its TLC-to-QLC mix remains about 70% to 30% for the current fiscal year. The company's QLC data-center product has completed customer qualifications and is ramping, according to Goeckeler.

Edge and consumer results

Edge revenue was $5.8 billion, up 7% sequentially. The company cited resilience in premium and mainstream markets, partly offset by contraction at the lower end of the market. Automotive and Internet-of-Things customers posted strong growth within the segment.

Consumer revenue was $397 million, down 29% sequentially as the market adjusted to higher pricing. Goeckeler said Sandisk continues to view consumer operations as a strategic asset because of its direct brand relationship with users and broad channel presence.

Management said PC and smartphone unit volumes remain under pressure, particularly at the low end of the market, but expects NAND exabyte demand to grow in each major end market next year as storage content per device rises. Goeckeler said the company expects PCs, smartphones and data center to all show positive NAND demand growth in calendar 2027 despite modest declines in unit volumes in some categories.

Long-term agreements and technology roadmap

During the quarter, Sandisk closed two new business model partnerships, or NBMs, which are longer-term customer arrangements intended to provide demand and financial visibility. Management said about 50% of its bits are under NBM arrangements for fiscal 2027 and about two-thirds are committed for fiscal 2028, with the proportion expected to rise further.

Visoso said 95% of the company's NBM agreements are with investment-grade companies that collectively generate about $130 billion in operating cash flow. The company said its NBM pipeline exceeds its available supply through the end of the decade.

Goeckeler said Sandisk is balancing requests from existing customers seeking additional supply with opportunities to add new partners. He added that the company has no plans to alter its previously discussed mid- to high-teens bit-growth plan, noting that wafer-fab transitions and equipment planning require substantial lead time.

On technology, Sandisk highlighted its BiCS8 NAND platform, along with planned BiCS9 and BiCS10 products. BiCS9 pairs the BiCS8 cell array with next-generation CMOS technology to raise interface performance, while BiCS10 is expected to include a 1-terabit TLC die and a 2-terabit QLC die.

The company also said it taped out its first High Bandwidth Flash, or HBF, memory die during the quarter and has begun fabrication. Sandisk expects to sample its first HBF-based products next calendar year. Goeckeler said the technology is intended to complement high-bandwidth memory by bringing NAND-class capacity closer to processors for inference workloads. HBF is not included in the company's long-term financial model, management said.

Margins, cash flow and outlook

Non-GAAP operating expenses were $513 million, or 4.7% of revenue, and non-GAAP operating margin was 80.4%, up from 79.2% in the preceding quarter. Cash flow from operations was $6.4 billion, while gross capital expenditures were $378 million, or 3.4% of revenue.

Sandisk expects gross capital spending to increase during the rest of fiscal 2027 and reach a mid-single-digit percentage of revenue for the year. The company ended the quarter with $5.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents and no debt.

Sandisk repurchased approximately 3.2 million shares for $5 billion in the first quarter. Over the past two quarters, it repurchased 6 million shares, representing roughly 4% of shares outstanding. Management reiterated its plan to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders while remaining debt-free and investing in its technology roadmap.

For fiscal second quarter 2027, Sandisk forecast revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and non-GAAP gross margin of 84.5% to 85.5%. The company projected pre-split non-GAAP earnings per share of $55 to $57, or $6.88 to $7.13 on an eight-for-one split-adjusted basis.

The board approved the eight-for-one stock split, with additional shares expected to be distributed Nov. 19 and split-adjusted trading expected to begin Nov. 20. Management said it expects calendar 2027 data-center demand to remain the industry's primary growth engine, with data center representing more than 55% of the market and bit demand rising about 40% year over year.

About Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK)

SanDisk Corporation offers flash storage solutions. The Company designs, develops and manufactures data storage solutions in a range of form factors using flash memory, controller, firmware and software technologies. The Company operates through flash memory storage products segment. Its solutions include a range of solid state drives (SSD), embedded products, removable cards, universal serial bus (USB), drives, wireless media drives, digital media players, and wafers and components. It offers SSDs for client computing applications, which encompass desktop computers, notebook computers, tablets and other computing devices.
